message.content:
This is an unconnectorized insulated cable of copper conductors, rated at 300 V, so it falls under heading 8544. Within that heading, 8544.42 covers conductors fitted with connectors and 8544.49 covers those not fitted with connectors. The 8544.49 subheading is split by voltage: 8544.49.10 is for voltage not exceeding 80 V, and 8544.49.30 is for 80 V to 1,000 V. The 8544.49.30 line is further divided into 8544.49.3000, a catch-all "Other" for 80 V to 1,000 V. The 300 V rating puts this cable in the 80–1,000 V range.

Newer HTSUS versions also have 8544.42.90 for connectorized cable, which does not apply here. I recall CBP rulings on CAT5e LAN cable classifying it in 8544.49.3000 (other, for a voltage over 80 V but not over 1,000 V, of copper). I am going from memory on those rulings.

The more specific 8544.49.10 line is for voltage not exceeding 80 V, so the 300 V rating rules it out. The choice therefore rests on the 300 V rating, and I am using 8544.49.30 with the final digits 00.

{"hts_code": "8544.49.3000", "reason": "Insulated copper data cable without connectors, rated at 300 V (over 80 V but not over 1,000 V), is classified in heading 8544, subheading 8544.49.30."}
